To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report the clinical and molecular findings in three patients with X-linked cerebral creatinuria from Israel.
we report three patients, two males, with creatine transporter defect, a novel mutation in the first patient, and two novel mutations, in the second and third patient.

we report three novel mutations in the SLCGA8 gene that result in a deficiency of the creatinetransporter and that we show that these three mutations are responsible for the observed creatinetransport deficiency in our three patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular basis of X-linked creatine deficiency syndrome.
the identification of novel mutations in the SLC8A gene in three Israeli patients.
the study of three patients from Israel with creatine transporter defect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

creatine transporter deficiency should be considered in the differential diagnosis of global developmental delays, particularly when accompanied by language apraxia, and when brain MRI reveals normal myelination but absent creatine peak in brain spectroscopy.
the diagnosis of creatine transporter defect should be considered in patients with language apraxia, developmental delay or microcephaly, even if brain imaging is normal.
creatine deficiency syndromes are caused by mutations in genes involved in the synthesis, transport and utilization of creatine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three patients with X-linked creatine deficiency had three different mutations in the SLC8A8 gene.

the creatine deficiency syndrome is an important cause of mental retardation and should be considered in patients presenting with developmental delays, particularly when there is a history of consanguinity.
the three patients had a novel mutation and a previously described one in the SLC8A8 gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mutations in the SLCG8A gene are a common cause for creatine deficiency syndrome and that functional studies of these mutations are helpful in establishing the diagnosis and understanding the pathogenesis of the disease.
creatine transporter deficiency is a rare but important cause of developmental disability in children.
mutations in SLC6A9 gene are associated with creatine transporter disorder.
